extracted.intended_audience: scientists, society organizers, and informed readers of Nature (early-20th-century scientific community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluative principles for scientific research practice, presentation, and the organisation/conduct of scientific meetings, as expressed in conference reports and presidential addresses. Emphasises empirical methods, experimental rigor, clear reporting, and practical arrangements for meetings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Health instruction by demonstration
rubrics_metrics.description: Instruction in the laws of health, cleanliness, dangers of impure food or water, and the evils of alcoholic abuse should not be given by lectures... but by actual demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teaching children about public health is most effective through practical demonstration rather than lecture; content should include hygiene, sanitation, nutrition, and alcohol risks, anticipating effects on the next generation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference organisation: convenience and clear directions
rubrics_metrics.description: Visitors on arrival found quite artistic street direction cards attached to the lamp-posts and tramway standards, and these, with the capital maps provided on the official ticket and bound with the local programme, gave clear and definite directions for all.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear signage, maps, and printed directions; plan local arrangements carefully to ensure visitor convenience and comfort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference social activities subordinate to scientific work
rubrics_metrics.description: The social side of the meeting has not by any means been neglected, but this has been kept quite subordinate to the real work — the advancement of science.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow social events (receptions, excursions, music) but ensure they do not overshadow or distract from the meeting's scientific programme.

rubrics_metrics.name: High character of proceedings through strong addresses and sectional papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The British Association has been fortunate in its choice of Leicester... because of the high character of its proceedings, initiated by the presidential address, and maintained in the special discourses... and the sectional papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select speakers and structure sections so presidential and special addresses set a high standard; quality and coherence of sectional papers sustain the meeting's scientific value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical emphasis: 'not to conquer Nature by talk, but by toil'
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt Baconian ideal: 'If any man makes it his delight and care — not so much to cling to and use past discoveries, as to penetrate to what is beyond them — not to conquer Nature by talk, but by toil... to gain sure and demonstrable knowledge.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritise experimental, demonstrable results over elegant speculation; value laborious empirical work that yields verifiable knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculative cosmogonies and fanciful theorising
rubrics_metrics.description: No more should Geology be inspired by that heedless spirit, which cares not to distinguish between fancy and fact!... The new Geology would have nothing to do with the search for cosmogonies and such like fancy foods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from pursuing grand speculative narratives unsupported by observation; focus on verifiable facts and sound inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not let preconceived views distort observation
rubrics_metrics.description: No more should observations be made through the distorting medium of preconceived fancies!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and interpret observations to minimise bias from preconceptions; ensure field and lab work are driven by objective data, not prior pet theories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental control and purification in combustion studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Erroneous ideas have gained currency from the use of impure gases, and hydrogen is still described as burning with a pale blue flame, although Stas long ago stated that if the gas is highly purified, and the air freed from dust, the flame even in a dark-room can only be discovered by feeling for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use highly purified reagents and remove contaminants (e.g., dust) to reveal true phenomena; control experimental impurities to avoid spurious structure or coloration in flames and other systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceptual clarity in defining key terms (ignition temperature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Temperature of ignition: 'the temperature at which the initial loss of heat due to conduction, &c., is equal to the heat evolved in the same time by the chemical reaction.' (van 't Hoff)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define central concepts precisely (e.g., ignition temperature as a balance of heat loss and heat evolution) and base experimental interpretation on clear theoretical definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution in mechanistic inference from isolated intermediates
rubrics_metrics.description: The isolation of an intermediate product in one set of circumstances is in itself no proof that this product is transitorily formed when the reaction is proceeding in another set of circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume that observed intermediates under one condition are necessarily present in other conditions; avoid over-interpreting isolated species as universal mechanistic steps without corroborating evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid literal reading of staged reaction schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: We must realise how far we are dealing with convenient devices and how far with ascertained facts... if we were to assume generally that because we can represent a chemical transaction as if it were due to a successive construction and destruction of a series of molecular edifices it actually does take such a course, we should... be making the same kind of mistake...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use staged reaction schemes as heuristic tools but test whether those stages genuinely occur under the studied conditions; be sceptical of treating schematic sequences as literal facts without direct evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribute flame structure to chemical causes, not experimental artefacts
rubrics_metrics.description: In a flame such as that of hydrogen or carbon monoxide... we should not expect to find a differentiation of structure... The presence of a very small quantity of free oxygen in carbon monoxide destroys the perfect simplicity of the single shell of blue flame... small quantities of gaseous impurities or of atmospheric dust give rise to features of structure and halos which have been frequently supposed to pertain to the flame of the combining gases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analysing flame structure (or analogous phenomena), distinguish intrinsic chemical/physical structure from effects introduced by impurities, small admixtures, or dust; ensure attribution of observed features is justified by controlled tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific reporting: present sure and demonstrable proofs
rubrics_metrics.description: At its meetings the leaders of the society announced what they had discovered, gave sure and demonstrable proofs of their discoveries, and showed in what direction the geological forces should be directed for the conquest of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reporting results, provide clear, reproducible evidence and argumentation; indicate how findings advance the field and suggest future directions grounded in demonstrable data.
